author: agent
text:
DEFECT, measured 2026-08-16 during the 0.54.0 close: this is presented as a read (`memway --json verify-change`, one of the seven JSON queries) and it WRITES. Fingerprinting .coord around one call on a repo whose tree had moved ahead of its map: five files rewritten - index/coordinates.json, index/edges.json, index/parse_cache.json, cache/coordinates.pkl, cache/edges.pkl. summary and attention, measured the same way in the same run, wrote nothing.

It shipped in 0.52.1 as the seventh --json query and was never added to READS in tests/test_read_fence.py, whose table holds before_edit, show, summary, at, lineage, viz, dig - and whose own docstring says "Every read surface, same measurement. Do not exempt one." The fence did not fail because the surface was never enrolled; CLAUDE.md lesson 3 says a new read surface goes under read_only() AND into that test, and only half of that happened.

How it surfaced: .coord/index/* turned up modified in a working tree where I had run no index. I first attributed it to memway_meta via MCP, which was wrong - isolated measurement shows memway_meta writes exactly ONE file, the note itself. Attribution from `git status` after a compound command is not measurement.

Sharper after 0.54.0: a "read" that reindexes can now perform the sketch migration, and the migration announces itself on stdout, which a --json caller has no reason to display.

Fix is read_only() plus enrolment in READS; both, or the next one hides the same way.

author: agent
text:
SUPERSEDES the DEFECT note below it. That defect is FIXED as of 0.54.1 and the note now reads as history, not as a description of this function. Read it for the reasoning; do not read it for what the code does.

What is true now: this is a PURE READ. Four write sites were removed - ix.save(), eb2.save(), the parse-cache refresh inside index() (via index(persist=False)), and the two cache-warming loaders (load_existing(write_cache=False) and EdgeBuilder.load(..., write_cache=False)). Suppressing only the first loader left cache/edges.pkl behind, which is how the earlier leaks in this file survived; there are exactly two on this path and missing either is a write. Verified on the published 0.54.1 wheel: fingerprinting a 14-file .coord around one call shows zero files written.

It also gained the thing it existed for: staled_knowledge, a list of {coordinate, qualname, channel, text} for the knowledge THIS change invalidated. Channel is required - superseding only heals when the fresh entry lands in the same channel, so a report omitting it sends the reader to write an entry that changes nothing.

Computed against the WORKING TREE, not the stored index. At the moment you would ask - edited, not re-indexed, not committed - the index still holds the old hashes and reports everything fresh.

Load-bearing and easy to undo by accident: it is now enrolled in READS in tests/test_read_fence.py, and test_every_json_query_is_enrolled_in_this_fence compares QUERIES to READS by NAME so no future query can ship unenrolled. The write here was once a DOCUMENTED exception ("THE ODD ONE OUT"); reversing it was deliberate, and the old test that recorded the write now asserts the opposite.

NOT wrapped in read_only(), which the fence proves is unnecessary today because this function never calls harvest_docs. If anyone adds one to this path, wrap it - the loader suppression protects only what it names.

author: agent
text:
Re-stated after 0.54.2. Everything the note below says is still true - pure read, staled_knowledge with a required channel, computed against the working tree, enrolled in READS. It went stale because the body gained one wrapper.

New: the whole load-and-verify sequence now runs inside `with read_only():`. That is belt AND braces and inert today, which the note below already predicted: the loader suppression makes this a pure read, but it protects only the two loaders it names. read_only() gates harvest_docs's docbindings baseline write, and this function does not call harvest_docs - so the wrapper changes nothing now and catches the case where somebody later adds one to this path. The previous note ended by saying "if anyone adds one to this path, wrap it"; this is that, done in advance rather than after the incident.

Do not remove it on the grounds that it does nothing. It does nothing on purpose, and the reason it does nothing is a fact about today's call graph, not a property of the function.

Also new in 0.54.2 and easy to miss: `memway verify-change .` is a CLI command now, not just MCP and --json. That door is what the pre-commit hook calls - a hook cannot pipe a JSON blob through sh readably - and its absence is part of why the supersede-before-you-finish rule went unfollowed by its own author twice in one evening.

author: cli
text: Re-confirmed after 0.54.2's display work. Everything the notes below say still holds - pure read, staled_knowledge with a required channel, computed against the working tree, enrolled in READS, wrapped in read_only(). The one change: the staled_knowledge scan now feeds meta.read_all through metadata.for_display before asking unsuperseded_stale, so it reports what a change invalidated using the same flag the ring and the panel use. One rule, three consumers.
